frequency_question: How often does a high-magnitude, contested immigration fee or wage rule reach final publication in the Federal Register within the first two years of an administration?
membership_rule: Includes economically significant USCIS/DHS rules involving extreme fee hikes or major structural visa overhauls proposed or finalized within 30 months of a presidential inauguration; excludes minor routine biennial fee adjustments.

cases.name: DHS H-1B Wage-Based Selection Rule (Trump 1st Term)

coverage_note: 3 named; represents the set of comparable high-salience immigration fee/selection rule finalization pushes in recent transitions.
known_gaps: Extreme outlier fee magnitudes like $103,265 have fewer direct precedents than standard fee doubling rules.
skeleton: Three major administrative cycles involving contested high-impact USCIS regulatory actions near presidential transitions
multiplier: 3 cases examined; 2 successfully reached final publication in the Federal Register despite litigation and tight timelines.
validity_reason: Valid through the duration of the current presidential term as administrative rulemaking behavior remains consistent.
